answer: Agents deposit bonded stake and prove membership in a Semaphore tree using polynomial identity commitments, then evaluate the epoch polynomial to derive a rate-limit nullifier. Reusing that nullifier for duplicate messages yields two Shamir shares; anyone can interpolate the signing secret and verify the violation, triggering instantaneous collateral slashing. The island of valid identities is thus protected by a cryptographic thread linking each vertex to one permitted message per epoch.
